final_answer: The deliverable is a PLAN-ONLY durable record (decisions/<dec-id>/plan.md) — no memory code is modified in this task, and the improve_* items are written as specifications for a follow-up pass (their 'Implement' verbs are read as 'specify in plan'). This resolves the one blocking contradiction the review flagged (no-code-modifications vs. 'Implement' verbs). The plan contains four accepted structural parts plus exactly TWO selected improvements: (1) a 16-row weakness→status(a/b/c)→verdict table where every status is backed by a concrete code citation in lib/memory.ps1, tools/memory-tail.ps1, lib/librarian.ps1, code-index, the driver context-builder, and [[PROJECT_*]] markers (highest-leverage anti-hallucination control: code is source of truth); (2) the improvement_constraints discipline read as a SELECTION rule (pick 2-3 reuse-only, no new layer/validator) which dissolves the 4-vs-2-3 conflict by naming the chosen two and deferring the fourth; (3) an evaluation of the 7 external-report priorities; (4) a deferred 'next-pass/fast-follow' list. The two selected improvements are: A) authority/trust labeling + disclaimer in the semantic recall render (Get-MemoryRecall), prefixing each item with its existing kind/trust and adding 'подсказка, не истина; код — источник правды; worklog/hypothesis проверять по файлам' — render-only, reuses typed-memory + trust/status, no validator; and B) auto evidence enrichment at marker write (ConvertFrom-ProjectMemoryMarker / Add-ProjectMemoryFromMarker) that backfills sha1+commit+line_text when evidence has 'file' but no 'sha1', reusing the existing evidence-fields and lazy-freshness subsystem — with 'lazy freshness only for recalled' FOLDED IN as a sub-item of B (it is a corollary that only fires once records carry sha1, so it is not a standalone third improvement). improve_kind_source_retention is REJECTED for this pass (single-proposal, 4th candidate breaking the 2-3 cap, and the largest blast radius since it mutates delete/dedup logic) and relocated into the deferred list. On the 7 priorities: authority-levels is the cheapest to implement (render-only) and is picked first; auto-evidence-enrichment is the precondition that makes lazy-freshness actually fire and is picked second; the memory_status.json heartbeat is named the cheapest FAST-FOLLOW but explicitly NOT adopted now because it would be a new monitoring layer, violating the no-new-mechanisms constraint (Foundation #2: harden, do not proliferate).

decisions.decision: Include a 16-row weakness→status(a/b/c)→verdict table in plan.md, with every status backed by a concrete code citation (lib/memory.ps1, tools/memory-tail.ps1, lib/librarian.ps1, code-index, driver context-builder, [[PROJECT_*]] markers).
decisions.rationale: Full consensus (A,B,C); the single highest-leverage anti-hallucination control — it forces each claimed improvement to be grounded in real code rather than in the external report's framing (code is source of truth). Cheap, fully reversible markdown.
alternatives_considered: Free-form prose summary without per-weakness code citations
Trusting the external report's 16 weaknesses at face value without code verification
decisions.risk: Low — markdown artifact, fully reversible; only residual risk is mis-mapping a weakness, mitigated by a strict 1:1 mapping to the report's enumerated set.
decisions.test: plan.md contains a 16-row table with columns weakness | status(a/b/c) | verdict-with-code-reference, and each status cites a file:symbol that proves it.

decisions.decision: Treat improvement_constraints as a SELECTION rule: choose exactly 2-3 candidate improvements that reuse existing mechanisms (typed memory, trust/status, freshness, librarian, evidence-fields) and add no new layer/validator; explicitly enumerate the chosen set and defer the rest.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B,C). This is the core discipline against scope creep and new infrastructure (Foundation #2). Reading it as a selection rule (not a mandate to ship all four candidates) dissolves the reviewer's 'major' contradiction once the plan names the two chosen and defers the fourth.
alternatives_considered: Relax the cap to 2-4 to fit all four candidates
decisions.risk: Low — the only residual is the 4-vs-2-3 gap, closed by deferring improve_kind_source_retention and folding activate_lazy_freshness into the enrichment item.
decisions.test: plan.md names exactly the two selected improvements, states for each which existing mechanism it reuses, and asserts no new layer/validator is added.

decisions.decision: Include an evaluation of all 7 external-report priorities, explicitly tagging authority-levels, auto-evidence-enrichment, lazy-freshness, and the memory_status heartbeat as present/partial/absent with relative cost, and naming the cheapest.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B,C). This is the analytical bridge that justifies the 2-3 selection — present/absent + cheapest-to-implement output is concrete and testable, and ties the report's priorities to the actual gap analysis.
alternatives_considered: Skip the priorities evaluation and present only own gap analysis
Evaluate only the 4 named priorities and ignore the other 3
decisions.risk: Low — pure analysis, no code touched.
decisions.test: plan.md has a priorities section addressing all 7 (at least the 4 named) with present/partial/absent + cost, identifies authority-levels as cheapest to implement and memory_status.json heartbeat as the cheapest fast-follow.

decisions.decision: Produce a single durable file decisions/<dec-id>/plan.md containing the weakness table, the 7-priorities evaluation, the two atomic improvement SPECIFICATIONS (file/change/acceptance/reused-mechanism/risk), the deferred list, and an explicit 'no new layers/validators and no memory code modified in this task' statement. The improve_* atoms are specifications for a follow-up pass; their 'Implement' verbs are reinterpreted as 'specify in plan'.
decisions.rationale: Judge MODIFY + micro-debate resolution: this closes the blocking contradiction between 'No memory code modifications' and the 'Implement' verbs in the improvement atoms by framing the whole task as plan-only.
alternatives_considered: Implement the improvements now in memory code
Split into plan plus immediate partial implementation
Emit multiple files instead of one
decisions.risk: Low — documentation only; the risk is scope-creep into implementation, mitigated by the explicit plan-only statement and by writing only under decisions/.
decisions.test: Exactly one new file under decisions/ exists; no file under lib/, tools/, or the driver is modified by this task.

decisions.decision: Select as improvement #1 (specified, not implemented): in the semantic recall render (Get-MemoryRecall), prefix each recalled item with its existing kind/trust (e.g. [worklog/observed]) and add a disclaimer header 'подсказка, не истина; код — источник правды; worklog/hypothesis проверять по файлам'. Reuses typed-memory + trust/status fields; adds no validator.
decisions.rationale: Best first pick (A,B). Render-only, fully reversible, lowest cost, directly mitigates the over-trust weakness, and is the cheapest realization of the authority-levels priority.
alternatives_considered: Add authority levels as a new metadata field on records
Filter low-trust items out of recall entirely instead of labeling them
decisions.risk: Low — render-only; the only risk is prompt verbosity/noise, mitigated by one compact disclaimer header plus terse inline kind/trust prefixes.
decisions.test: Spec acceptance: the recall block prefixes each entry with its kind/trust and shows one disclaimer header, visibly separating evidence-backed entries from low-trust ones.

decisions.decision: Select as improvement #2 (specified, not implemented): at marker write (ConvertFrom-ProjectMemoryMarker / Add-ProjectMemoryFromMarker), when evidence has 'file' but no 'sha1', resolve the path, compute sha1, and backfill sha1+commit+line_text into the evidence object — reusing the existing evidence-fields and lazy-freshness subsystem, with no new evidence service or validator. FOLD IN activate_lazy_freshness as a sub-item: once records carry sha1, the existing lazy-freshness check (run only on recalled items) detects staleness.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B) and the precondition that makes lazy-freshness staleness actually fire. activate_lazy_freshness is a corollary (records need sha1 to be checkable) with the vaguest standalone acceptance test, so it is bundled here rather than counted as a third improvement — keeping the selected set at two.
alternatives_considered: Keep activate_lazy_freshness as a standalone third improvement
Eager freshness on all stored memory instead of lazy on recalled only
decisions.risk: Medium — more moving parts (path resolution, commit lookup), reversibility medium. Mitigate: enrich best-effort, skip silently when the path is unresolved or git is unreachable in the sandbox, and make no behavior change when sha1 is already present.
decisions.test: Spec acceptance: a marker written with a file ref but no sha1 gets evidence.sha1 (plus commit+line_text) populated at write; a later file change flags the recalled entry stale via the existing freshness mechanism; freshness runs only on recalled items.

decisions.decision: Include a 'next-pass / fast-follow' deferred list (supersede subject/predicate, recall-replay harness, global context-budget manager, code-index freshness banner, decisions normalized cache, fast-lane safety pack, end-of-task candidate block, AND the relocated kind/source-aware retention). Name memory_status.json heartbeat as the cheapest fast-follow but explicitly do NOT adopt it now because it would be a new monitoring layer.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A,B). This is the governance that enforces the no-new-mechanisms constraint and is the correct home for the rejected improve_kind_source_retention, keeping the active set to the two render/evidence improvements.
alternatives_considered: Adopt the memory_status.json heartbeat now as the third improvement
Omit a deferred list and silently drop the heavier ideas
decisions.test: plan.md lists the deferred items including kind/source-aware retention, names memory_status.json heartbeat as the cheapest fast-follow, and states the reason it is excluded this pass (new monitoring layer).

Non-consensus (proposal B only), it is the 4th candidate that breaks the exactly-2-3 selection cap, and it mutates deletion/dedup logic — the largest blast radius of all candidates, conflicting with the no-new-mechanisms/small-atoms and plan-only constraints. red_team_findings.what: Improvement #3 is a no-op built on an UNVERIFIED precondition that is one readable line in the file the decision cites. It frames the work as 'confirm/flip restaleOnSha1Mismatch to default-on in Get-MemoryConfig' and parks the answer in open_questions ('Current default of restaleOnSha1Mismatch ... if already on, #3 collapses into verification-only'). The actual code: restaleOnSha1Mismatch = $true AND verifyOnRecall = $true are BOTH defaults in Get-MemoryConfig (lib/memory.ps1:381-382), and a repo-wide search shows NO config.json override (only matches are inside the decision's own artifacts). verifyOnRecall is the gate that actually triggers Test-MemoryHitFreshness (lib/memory.ps1:927). So lazy freshness is already fully activated; #3 changes zero code and zero config.
red_team_findings.why: Directly violates the task's binding constraint 'Do NOT trust the external analysis at face value; verify against actual code (code is source of truth)' — the decision failed to read line 382 of a file it references dozens of times, and propagated proposal_B's inverted precedence reading. It also hollows the 'select THREE coupled improvements' COUNT RULING: only TWO improvements (#1 render, #2 enrichment) carry content, so the operator-review gate for 'atom smallness / no padding' is presented with an empty atom dressed as real. The decision itself flags this in open_questions yet never resolved it despite the answer being trivially checkable.

red_team_findings.what: The freshness/stale signal never reaches the render path Improvement #1 targets. #1 dresses up Get-MemoryRecall (lib/memory.ps1:1043-1067), which renders raw '- (pct%) text' and never reads status/freshness nor calls Format-ProjectMemoryHits -RequireFresh. The lazy stale-check (#3) and -RequireFresh exclusion live only on the TYPED pack path (Get-ProjectContextPack / Format-ProjectMemoryHits, lib/project-context.ps1:215-228). The two paths are disjoint.
red_team_findings.why: Undercuts the decision's central claim that the three improvements are 'coupled' and 'reuse exactly these mechanisms.' After shipping #1+#2+#3, the generic semantic block (#1's surface, and the exact subject of weaknesses #1/#14 'memory treated as truth') will still surface stale records with no stale marker, because Get-MemoryRecall ignores status entirely. #1 adds [kind/trust] labels but the freshness benefit it implies does not flow there.

red_team_findings.what: Improvement #2's chosen location contradicts its own acceptance criteria. The decision places enrichment in ConvertFrom-ProjectMemoryMarker / Add-ProjectMemoryFromMarker (lib/project-context.ps1:243-274), which is invoked synchronously from driver/84-loop-reply-markers.ps1:127. The repo's own commit history (and the decision's open_questions) confirm the coder sandbox at the synchronous marker-reply path 'cannot reach .git'. SHA1 (file read) works there, but the acceptance demands backfilling 'sha1+commit+line_text' — the commit lookup needs git and will fail in that location.
red_team_findings.why: proposal_B explicitly mitigated this by running enrichment 'only on the detached memory-tail path' (where .git is reachable). The final decision moved it to the synchronous path and left the reachability conflict unresolved in open_questions rather than fixing the atom. As written, #2's acceptance ('commit populated on write') is unsatisfiable at the specified call site — an internal inconsistency an operator reviewing for integrity should catch.

red_team_findings.what: The 'librarian' reuse claim is unsupported. Success_test 6 requires the plan to demonstrate reuse/strengthening of 'librarian' among the named mechanisms, and section 0 claims reuse of 'existing librarian/recall renderers.' But no chosen improvement touches lib/librarian.ps1: #1 edits Get-MemoryRecall (in lib/memory.ps1), #2 edits lib/project-context.ps1, #3 is config. All librarian-related weaknesses (W9, W12) were deferred.
red_team_findings.why: Section 0 conflates the recall renderer Get-MemoryRecall (which lives in lib/memory.ps1) with the librarian (lib/librarian.ps1) to manufacture a 'librarian reused' claim. Against success_test 6's explicit enumeration including 'librarian,' this is a partial miss / misstatement that the no-new-mechanisms framing leans on.

red_team_findings.what: The audit status column violates the specified value set. Success_test 3 requires each row categorized as 'a', 'b', or 'c' (a single letter). Rows 1.3, 1.8, and 1.13 use 'b/c' (two values), which is outside the specified domain.
red_team_findings.why: Literal nonconformance with the output_format and success_test 3. Minor, but the operator review checks 'integrity' of the table; a hybrid 'b/c' bucket is exactly the kind of ambiguity that defeats the a/b/c triage the contract asked for.

red_team_findings.what: Imprecise code references that the decision presents as proof of 'already built.' It states Test-MemoryHitFreshness is 'wired into Search-Memory at :928' / 'invoked from Search-Memory at :928,' but line 928 is inside Set-MemoryHitsLastRecalled; Search-Memory only reaches it indirectly at lines 969/1039. The check is additionally gated by verifyOnRecall and throttled by RecallFlushMinIntervalSec (lib/memory.ps1:916-928), and it mutates/saves the reloaded store records, so staling takes effect on the NEXT recall, not the current render.
red_team_findings.why: The decision's whole redirection ('three priorities already built, don't rebuild') rests on these citations, and the task demanded file:line accuracy. The omitted throttle/next-recall semantics also weaken Improvement #3's acceptance wording ('a file change causes the recalled record to be flagged stale [and excluded]'), which will not hold on the first recall after an edit.
